chapter_theme: The one song at Then Kadambanthurai (தென்கடம்பந்துறை) on the Kaveri: women's eyes that outdo every standard of comparison and the gold given to them, against a plea to reach the red feet at dawn and dusk; the praise lists the shrines and hearts Murugan dwells in and the river born from Agastya's water-pot.

922.reading: The poet sets women's eyes against the sea, Kama, the bee, the carp and kendai fish, Yama, the lotus, poison and the vel that pierced the hill, eyes that roam here and there, redden at the corners and are packed with deceit, and asks whether, having given much red gold to such women, he will settle at dawn and dusk, free of ties, so that mind, speech and body draw near Murugan's red feet. The praise lists the kadamba garland, the twelve shoulders, the six faces, mantra and tantra, Palani, Parangundram, Senthil and the hearts of true devotees, Siva with serpent, Ganga and moon who bows to him as guru, and the shrine on the river that came from the sage's water-pot on the Kudagu hill.
922.nuance: செந்தனம் தந்து, giving red gold, makes the women courtesans. த்ரிவித கரணங்களும் ... குறுகும்வகை: the three instruments of mind, speech and body are to approach the feet together. குடகு, the sage's கமண்டலம் and the river point to the Kaveri born from Agastya's water-pot; the part played by சங்கரன் in that line is not clear to me.

links.note: 922 asks that its த்ரிவித கரணங்கள், the three instruments of mind, speech and body, approach Murugan's red feet, free of ties (தொந்தம் அற்று). Tirumanthiram 2612 says strong karma kindles through மன வாக்கு காயம் and does not last when they stand straight. The Tirumanthiram supplies the reason the three instruments matter; the Thiruppugazh turns them toward the feet.
